messages:
nina (support): headsup — Acme is seeing intermittent 599s and long requests when sending a few small embedding batches. They hit a retry loop in the SDK and billing spiked. Repro steps pasted below. Can infra/runtime take a look?

jordan (eng-infra): thanks. can you paste the exact request + trace-id? any pattern (region/time)?

nina (support): trace: tr_8f3c9a1b, region: us-west, started ~2026-03-15T14:02Z. customer says fail rate ~20% for bursts of 8–12 inputs. quick repro they used: 
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"embed-lite","inputs":["a","b","c","d","e","f","g","h","i","j","k"]}'
```
response: HTTP/1.1 599 Connection truncated, body empty. SDK logs show repeated 599 then immediate retry, leading to double billing.

lee (eng-runtime): odd status. 599 usually means upstream closed stream mid-chunk. can you confirm whether they had multiplexing / http2 multiplexing on in the SDK?

nina (support): they use our JS SDK v1.12, default multiplexing on. customer tried turning retries off and saw fewer duplicate charges but still some 599s.

jordan (eng-infra): I'm running the local reproducer against us-west now with the same payload. leaving a minimal repro script below so we all run the same thing: 
```js
// repro.js
const sdk = require('@redwood/sdk');
await sdk.init({ region: 'us-west' });
await sdk.embeddings.create({ model: 'embed-lite', inputs: Array.from({length:11}, (_,i)=>String(i)) });
```
I see 3/10 failures with 599 and an upstream error in the logs: "write: broken pipe" around the time the response would stream.

alex (sre): noticed a recent proxy patch to the edge fleet that adjusted http2 window/keepalive behavior in us-west at 2026-03-15T13:20 (deploy id edge-proxy-2026-03-15-1320). rolling back that patch on a canary would be quick to test. suspect it aggressively closed idle streams during small bursts and left the backend mid-send.

lee (eng-runtime): if rollback is quick we should try. mitigation options while rolling back: 1) recommend customer set SDK option multiplex=false and reduce batch size to 5; 2) temporarily disable client-side retries or use exponential backoff with jitter; 3) route customer traffic to eu-west via policy (if latency acceptable).

deploy-bot: rollback started: edge-proxy-2026-03-15-1320 -> edge-proxy-2026-03-14-2107 on us-west canary (hosts: proxy-uw1-2).

jordan (eng-infra): can confirm canary rollback applied to proxy-uw1-2. re-running repro against canary: 10/10 success, no 599s. logs show stable http2 frames and no EPIPE.

lee (eng-runtime): looks like rollback mitigates. plan: roll back cluster-wide for us-west and monitor p95. I'll coordinate with deploy team.

nina (support): messaging customer now: "we identified an edge proxy change that can cause truncated responses for certain small-batch embedding bursts. We've rolled back the change to canary and are rolling back the us-west fleet; please try again with multiplex disabled and smaller batches as a temporary workaround. We will credit affected requests. Investigating root cause and will follow up in 2 hours." :white_check_mark:

alex (sre): rolling back us-west fleet now, will post update when complete.

deploy-bot: rollback complete on us-west (edge fleet) at 2026-03-15T14:22Z.

jordan (eng-infra): post-rollback sanity run: 50 repeated repro attempts => 0/50 599, mean latency unchanged. capturing p95 token latency now.

lee (eng-runtime): root cause summary so far: http2/keepalive window change in edge proxy was closing streams prematurely under small-batch load patterns, which caused upstream connections to be torn during chunked responses. That manifested as 599 and triggered SDK retry loops. We'll do a deeper postmortem on the proxy patch logic (window sizing + idle timeouts).

nina (support): customer updated: they tested 3x and all succeeded. promised a billing credit and will follow up with final confirmation after 24h. thanks team for the quick turnaround.

jordan (eng-infra): next actions: 1) postmortem on proxy patch and add a canary test that reproduces small-batch embed bursts; 2) SDK doc note about multiplexing edge cases and recommended safe defaults for embeddings; 3) billing reconciliation for duplicate/charged retries.

lee (eng-runtime): agreed. I'll open the RFC for proxy fix + automated regression test.

nina (support): closing loop with customer and marking thread for follow-up after 24h. if anything regresses ping this thread. :pray:
